Target: a Cox model

target_cox.Rd

Builds the target of an analysis whose outcome is a follow-up time with an event indicator: the (stratified) Cox proportional-hazards model $$h(t \mid z) = h_{0s}(t)\, \exp(z^\top\beta),$$ with a baseline hazard \(h_{0s}\) for each stratum \(s\) and coefficients \(\beta\) shared by all strata. The target sets the likelihood \(\ell(\theta)\) in the objective of cv.bregsurv(): the log partial likelihood of your data.

target_cox() checks your data and stores it; it fits nothing. Pass the result to cv.bregsurv() (or bregsurv()) as target.

Usage

target_cox(
  time,
  event,
  z,
  stratum = NULL,
  ties = c("none", "breslow", "exact"),
  score = "linear"
)

Arguments

time

Observed follow-up time of each subject: the event time when event = 1, the censoring time when event = 0. Positive numbers, with no missing values.

event

Event indicator of each subject: 1 if the event was observed, 0 if the subject was censored. Numeric, logical, or the characters "0" and "1". A factor, a missing value or any other code (such as a competing event coded 2) is refused.

z

Covariates: a numeric matrix, or a data frame of numeric columns, with one row per subject and one named column per covariate. The column names are how an external model's coefficients and an external cohort's records are matched to your covariates (unnamed columns are called Z1, Z2, ...). Code categorical covariates as numbers, for instance as indicator columns, first. Missing values are refused.

stratum

Optional stratum of each subject, any labels (for instance the centre). Each stratum has its own baseline hazard and the coefficients are shared. NULL puts every subject in one stratum.

ties

How tied event times enter the partial likelihood:

  • "none" (the default): subjects who fail at the same time are taken in the order of your data;

  • "breslow": Breslow's approximation, in which everyone still at risk at a tied event time is in its risk set; available with every divergence and penalty;

  • "exact": Cox's exact partial likelihood; available with the Kullback-Leibler divergence and no penalty.

The three coincide when no two events share a time.

score

The form of the risk score: "linear" (the default), the linear predictor \(z^\top\beta\), or a neural network specified by nn_score() (requires the torch package; the Kullback-Leibler divergence only).

Value

An object of class "bregsurv_target", a list with

type

"cox".

time, event, stratum

The checked follow-up times, event indicators and strata.

z

The covariates as a numeric matrix with column names.

ties, score

The settings.

n

The number of subjects.

See also

cv.bregsurv(); the other targets, target_ncc() and target_discrete(); the releases, release_records(), release_coef(), release_score() and release_model().

Examples

data(ExampleData_lowdim)
tr <- ExampleData_lowdim$train
target_cox(time = tr$time, event = tr$status, z = tr$z)
#> Target: Cox model
#>   100 subjects, 6 covariates, 29 events

# with strata: each centre has its own baseline hazard
data(ExampleData_indi)
int <- ExampleData_indi$internal
target_cox(time = int$time, event = int$status, z = int$z, stratum = int$stratum)
#> Target: Cox model
#>   500 subjects, 10 covariates, 355 events, 10 strata

# follow-up recorded at visits, so many event times are tied
data(ExampleData_ties)
ti <- ExampleData_ties$train
target_cox(time = ti$time, event = ti$status, z = ti$z, ties = "breslow")
#> Target: Cox model
#>   100 subjects, 6 covariates, 29 events
#>   tied event times: breslow
